mechaber/1:main: Birkas Hamazon on the Third Cup. And in it one section: Afterwards they pour the third cup and bless upon it Birkas Hamazon and Borei peri hagafen and one drinks it while reclining, and one does not bless a berachah achronah upon it, and one does not drink wine between it and the fourth cup: {Rama: However, from the third cup one may drink many times and all of it counts as one drinking, even though he interrupted in between (Maharil, Mahari, and Tashbetz}.} It is a mitzvah to respond after zimmun: {Rama: And the greatest among them says Hodu and Ana and the others answer after him (Kol Bo). And the greatest may give permission to a minor (Maharil}. And one may join for zimmun for the purpose of Hallel even though he did not eat with them. And the custom is that the baal habayis recites Birkas Hamazon on Passover night, as it is said good-eyed is he who shall be blessed — and he is called good-eyed because he said All who are hungry, let them come and eat, etc.}
baer-heitev/1:א: (א) They pour [the cup]. And one must rinse and wash if the cup is not clean — see Chok Yaakov.
baer-heitev/1:ב: (ב) Wine — the same applies to other intoxicating beverages; but a beverage that does not intoxicate, one is permitted to drink [between cups]. Taz.
baer-heitev/1:ג: (ג) He may [drink many times]. Nevertheless he should not drink so much that he becomes intoxicated. Chok Yaakov.
baer-heitev/1:ד: (ד) And the greatest [among them] — Maharil wrote a minor does not say Hodu but does say Ana, and that is l'chatchila; but there is not so much stringency since women may join for this — see Magen Avraham; and women are also obligated in this Hallel — see Chok Yaakov.
baer-heitev/1:ה: (ה) The baal habayis — even if he has a guest — see siman 491. Chok Yaakov.
beer-hagolah/1:ב: (ב) I cited it above in siman 473 seif 2
beer-hagolah/1:ד: (ד) In the name of Midrash Tehillim
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (Sak 1) How many times when his mind was full, he was distracted and needed to bless, and he was like adding on the cups. And he also wrote in the 19th chapter of the Hebrew the Gemara, section 7, that there is a dambarach on the glass, as it is added there, section 9 of the DKKF, one should drink at once more than a fourth:
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) How many times. When he thought about it at the time of blessing, he said:
magen-avraham/1:ב: (ב) After zimmun — it implies in Tur specifically for Hallel of mitzvah one returns; but Birkat Hamazon his law is as other days of the year — see siman 137; and some wish to combine also Birkat Hamazon, and if so he must not eat the afikoman at home but in the place where he blesses, as siman 484 — for if he eats afikoman alone it is like eating two Pesach offerings; and so all in Avudraham, for this zimmun is like a passing mitzvah and permitted to uproot, as siman 478 seif 2 in Hagahah; and it appears even for those who forbid eating two meals at night, as siman 484 — that is specifically when he blessed Birkat Hamazon in the middle; but when he did not bless Birkat Hamazon in the middle, even though he went elsewhere, it is like one meal (and so in Tur); nevertheless per Maharil siman 478 it is forbidden to leave in the middle of his meal unless he blessed Birkat Hamazon first — see there; and we practice as Rama wrote, and Tur wrote that even in Hallel it suffices that they answer after him — his wife and sons; and so Tosafot Sukkah 38a wrote that women are obligated in this Hallel; and Maharil wrote a minor does not say Hallel — but I say he answers after him what he says; and Mahariv wrote: even though they say in the Gemara let it be a curse to one who treats his Creator lightly to make such agents — that is specifically at the beginning of the chapter; and in Agudah in Sotah siman 21 — if a minor says please say etc., he answers after him what he says; and at the end of Pesachim it is written if there are not twenty-one adults, both say Hallel; and Agur wrote mitzvah with three adults on both nights — end; and certainly l'chatchila one should do mitzvah from the best; but there is not so much stringency, for women also join, as stated.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) They pour for him the third cup — and it requires rinsing and washing if it is not clean; and even one who is not careful all year to see if it is clean, nevertheless on this night he should be careful because of hidur mitzvah.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) And he blesses upon it Birkas Hamazon — even if he blesses alone, and even per the general view that Birkas Hamazon does not require a cup, nevertheless since the Sages enacted to drink four cups on this night, one should make a mitzvah with each and every cup; therefore they adjoin the third cup to Birkas Hamazon [Gemara].
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) And he drinks it while reclining — and if he drank without reclining, if he returns and drinks, see above in siman 472 seif 7 and in Hagahah.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) And he does not bless a berachah achronah upon it — even if he drank the entire revi'it, since he relies on the final blessing he will bless on the fourth cup.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (ה) And he does not drink wine — lest he become intoxicated and sleep and not complete the Hallel; and some wrote the reason is lest it appear he is adding to the cups; and the Acharonim wrote it is not specifically wine — the same applies to other intoxicating beverages; nevertheless if it does not intoxicate it is permitted, when it was not strong wine from the country; if it was strong wine from the country one should be strict and be concerned for the second reason, that it appears like adding to the cups.
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) However, from the third cup, etc. — for the first reason, because of intoxication, it certainly does not apply, for he does not drink more than four cups; and for the reason that it appears like adding, also there is none, for it is only one cup; nevertheless if after drinking most of a revi'it he did not intend to drink more and afterward changed his mind to drink more, the view of Magen Avraham and Chok Yaakov is that since he must bless upon it anew, it appears like adding to the cups; see above in siman 472 in Biur Halacha what we wrote on this.
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (ז) How many times — nevertheless if the cup is very much larger than usual, he should not drink all of it so he does not become intoxicated [Acharonim].
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (ח) That he interrupted in between — meaning after he drank most of a revi'it at first, he interrupted much more than the time of eating a peras.
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (ט) After zimmun — the Acharonim agreed that this zimmun is not regarding Birkas Hamazon, for because of this he is not obligated to return more than other days of the year; here it deals with Hallel, that it is a mitzvah to beautify saying Hallel with three so one says to two Hodu and they answer the verse after it; and the one they call to this zimmun should not eat, drink, or assist in blessing the zimmun blessing, only hear Hodu and answer with them and return home; and in this too they agreed that even though it is a mitzvah from the best to say Hallel with three adult men, therefore if he has in his house at one table a man of obligation, certainly it is proper to join him for saying Hodu; nevertheless there is not so much stringency, for he may do this with his wife and sons (and if his sons are minors, see below) — meaning he says and they answer [and so too his wife may say Hodu, for women are also obligated in this Hallel as they are obligated in the four cups; and Chok Yaakov wrote that per what we practice to say Hodu with pleasant melody, one should be concerned for what we say in the Gemara 'women sing and men answer' like fire in flax]. And if he wishes to return after zimmun for Birkas Hamazon and go to his neighbor to bless there, he should not eat the afikoman at home, for he will need to eat something there to join for Birkas Hamazon, and it is forbidden to eat after the afikoman anything; and the afikoman itself is forbidden to divide and eat in two places, as above in siman 478; rather he eats the afikoman where he makes zimmun and blesses there, and also drinks the cup there and remains there until completing the seder; and if he wishes he may return home after Birkas Hamazon and complete the Hallel and drink the fourth cup; but nevertheless they do not now practice to go eat the afikoman in another house; and it is better to bless alone at home than go in the middle of his meal to another house and seek zimmun. Indeed if he wishes to beautify and fulfill everything from the best and does not have in his house a complete zimmun of three people, he should see to invite from the start to the meal some guest so he has a complete zimmun for Birkas Hamazon and also for saying Hodu.
mishnah-berurah/1:י: (י) He says Hodu and Ana, etc. — it is only a mitzvah l'chatchila and not for voiding [Peri Chadash].
mishnah-berurah/1:כ: (כ) And the others answer after him — and if there are not twenty-one years, both say Hodu [Acharonim].
mishnah-berurah/1:ל: (ל) To give a minor permission — that he says so they do not sleep and also to educate them in mitzvos; and this is specifically for saying Ana, because they answer after him that very verse, but not for Hodu.
mishnah-berurah/1:מ: (מ) That the baal habayis blesses — even if he has a guest; nevertheless there is no stringency if another blessed [Chok Yaakov].
turei-zahav/1:א: (א) And he drinks it while reclining — and if he did not drink while reclining, it is explained in siman 472. Maharshal wrote: one requires rinsing and washing — this is the view of all Acharonim; and even one not careful all year to see if the cup is clean, nevertheless on this night he should be careful for hidur mitzvah.
turei-zahav/1:ב: (ב) And he does not drink wine, etc. — the reason in Yerushalmi is lest he become intoxicated and be unable to complete the Hallel; and they challenged: but is he not already intoxicated? They answer: wine during the meal does not intoxicate. Rashbam wrote; and it should be said that the same applies to wine before the meal that does not intoxicate — from this it appears to me he may not drink mead called ma'ad either, since it too intoxicates; but other beverages that do not intoxicate are permitted.
turei-zahav/1:ג: (ג) It is a mitzvah to respond after zimmun — Tur wrote on this, and so it was stated in Midrash Tehillim: one who recites Hallel needs three, that one says to two Hodu; and Avudraham wrote they do not practice thus; and if because of Hodu, three suffice with his wife and sons who reached education — end. Explanation: Rosh wrote at the end of chapter Afikoman there is proof Birkas Hamazon requires a cup specifically with three — for if even alone, why did they say obligation of four cups on Pesach night? The Birkas Hamazon cup every day requires a cup — rather certainly with three specifically it requires a cup, and on Pesach one must return after three to have four cups; afterward Rosh rejected this proof, for nevertheless there are four cups together on this day; therefore Tur wrote in his name and the world did not practice thus. Explanation: from Birkas Hamazon side, even alone needs a cup; and also for Hodu his wife and sons suffice; and it appears what Tur wrote mitzvah to return after zimmun — he did not intend at all for Birkas Hamazon, for he already ruled in siman 482 that Birkas Hamazon requires a cup even alone; rather certainly from Hodu alone he said so, as he concludes in the name of Midrash Tehillim — that they call him to zimmun, and the one who comes to zimmun should not eat, drink, or assist in blessing zimmun, for he already blessed; only hear Hodu and answer with them and return home; and this too is Shulchan Aruch's intent writing mitzvah to return after zimmun — zimmun for Hodu; and as Rama wrote on this that the greatest says Hodu; and although Rosh wrote wife and sons suffice, nevertheless it is better with three obligated men for this; but for Birkas Hamazon zimmun it is not proper to call one from another house to bless with him if he did not eat here — for on what will he assist to bless? And even if he wishes to drink here to join zimmun it is not proper: if he ate afikoman at home he may not drink here; if he did not eat afikoman at home it will be forbidden afterward to eat afikoman at home since he already blessed — therefore the practical case is only that he not eat afikoman at home but eat it here, and he need not bless motzi here a second time as siman 484 seif 2; and see siman 484; and this is not forbidden because of two groups, for this is only once he began afikoman; but from the mitzvah side of eating at the meal there is no prohibition of places, as Rama in siman 478 — changing before this is not an interruption, and the same for changing place; after he eats afikoman here he blesses with them and remains until completing the seder; if he wishes he may return home after Birkas Hamazon and say Hallel with them and drink the fourth cup — if he has three at home besides himself for zimmun; if not, certainly forbidden to ruin his zimmun; and per what Maharshal wrote, the complaint of Maharshal and Maharal of Prague is settled, who bring that he would need to bless again at home — they do not now practice eating afikoman in another house; also not required for Birkas Hamazon zimmun, for we practice cup even alone; and if for Hodu, Rosh already wrote wife and sons suffice; and trouble to call from another house is not required unless he has at another table an obligated man — join him for Hodu only — and no more; so it appears correct per our custom.
